$comment: Machine-readable address catalog for Extra Utilities G1 (BZR 2.2.301).
$comment2: Each entry carries the known hardcoded address alongside a 'pattern' field.
$comment3: Patterns are IDA-style byte sequences (?? = wildcard byte). Where no pattern has
$comment3b: been derived the field is null and a 'note' says why.
$comment3c: pattern_kind 'code': the pattern starts at 'address' (functions, hook and patch sites). pattern_kind 'reference': the pattern is a unique instruction sequence elsewhere that contains the address bytes (data globals, vftables, strings); 'note' names the matching instruction.
$comment4: Verify with: python tools/qualify_bzr_build.py <exe> --catalog. Feature code names these addresses through src/Util/EngineAddresses.generated.h (python tools/generate_engine_addresses.py; --check in CI); tools/validate_hardening.py fails when src/ spells an engine-range literal anywhere else.
$comment4b: Derive new signatures from the GOG executable; the Steam executable is SteamStub-packed.

target.note: BZR is a 32-bit process. All absolute addresses are virtual addresses in the default load image.

dummynode.description: The executable's Lua 5.1 dummynode_. EXU links its own Lua core against the game's lua_State, and Lua5.1-BZR/src/ltable.c hard-codes this address as dummynode so both cores agree on the empty-table sentinel. If it moves, EXU's luaH_resize frees the host's static node (heap corruption).

setnodevector.description: Lua 5.1 setnodevector; the size==0 branch stores t->node = dummynode. Required runtime anchor: its signature embeds the dummynode address, so a build where the address moved fails before EXU creates any table.
setnodevector.note: Unique in GOG 2.2.301 .text (verified 2026-09-27). The executable has 7 imm32 references to dummynode, all in the Lua core.

saveDirectory.description: The engine's save directory. The startup routine (0x00618FF0, called from WinMain) fills it once with _getcwd() + "\save", before any Lua runs, and nothing writes it afterwards. SaveShellGame builds <saveDirectory>\game<slot>.sav from it and SaveGame creates it before writing. src/Util/OS.cpp reads it (behind the runtime build gate) to build exu.SaveGame slot paths; SavePathPolicy.h's BuildSlotSavePath fails closed when it is empty, unterminated or not an absolute drive path.

The next global the executable references is 0x02CEFFE0, so the buffer is 0x1000 bytes.

WeaponFireHeld.description: State byte of the 'weapon_fire' command (command table 0x008EB888, type 1 = held): nonzero while the fire bind is down at the last input poll. SelectTrack.description: Redux soundtrack track/loop selector, void __cdecl (int track, int loopFirst, int loopSkip, int loopLast), on exact GOG Redux 2.2.301. The world loader FUN_00780160 reads [World] MusicTrack/MusicLoopFirst/MusicLoopSkip/MusicLoopLast from the .trn and passes them here in that order; the shell (FUN_007BEFD0, FUN_004341C0) calls it with one track in every slot to loop a single track. It calls Music::Stop (0x00437A70) only when the track differs from the current one, then stores the four values; the end-of-track advancer FUN_00437B00 consumes them. Selects only: playback starts in Music::Start. Unique on the GOG image with every absolute and rel32 operand wildcarded.

Start.description: Redux soundtrack start, void __cdecl (void), on exact GOG Redux 2.2.301 -- the real playback entry, not the legacy _StartMusic 0x00406670, which is a dead identity stub on this build (live_scan_findings_20260706.md #17). If nothing is playing it formats the selected track with "%02d.ogg", sizes and loads it through the resource layer (0x00481A60/0x00481AF0), opens it through the thunk 0x0043F9B0 to OggManager::Setup (0x0043F050, which logs "Starting Music Playback Index %d"), and when the options music volume byte is non-zero sets the playing flag and calls the thunk 0x0043F9E0 to OggManager::Play (0x0043F320) and the volume setter FUN_00437800. Called by the mission start FUN_00617110, the shell FUN_007BEFD0 and the advancer FUN_00437B00. A no-op while music is already playing. Unique on the GOG image with every absolute and rel32 operand wildcarded.

Stop.description: Redux soundtrack stop, void __cdecl (void), on exact GOG Redux 2.2.301 -- the real stop, not the legacy _StopMusic 0x004068E0 stub. If an Ogg slot is open it calls the thunk 0x0043FA20 to OggManager::Pause (0x0043F5C0) while playing, then the thunk 0x0043FA60 to OggManager::Release (0x0043F780), releases the "%02d.ogg" resource (0x00481990), and clears the slot, playing and paused flags. Called by Music::SelectTrack on a track change, by the mission teardown FUN_00618370 and FUN_00439FB0, and by the advancer before moving to the next track. Idempotent. Unique on the GOG image with every absolute and rel32 operand wildcarded.

Pause.description: Redux soundtrack pause, void __cdecl(void), on exact GOG Redux 2.2.301. Identified in live_scan_findings_20260706.md #17 and the matching GOG corpus: pause retains the Ogg stream and sets the paused flag only while started and not paused; resume clears it only while started and paused. The released-build layout is anchored to the already verified unique Music::Stop entry, at the recorded negative offset. This is a fixed-layout resolve, not a newly qualified standalone signature; reject on build or anchor mismatch. New runtime validation is still required before release.

The released-build layout is anchored to the already verified unique Music::Stop entry, at the recorded negative offset. This is a fixed-layout resolve, not a newly qualified standalone signature; reject on build or anchor mismatch. New runtime validation is still required before release.

ResourceSize.description: Resource-layer file size query, int __cdecl (const char* name), on exact GOG Redux 2.2.301, taken from the first call in Music::Start, which passes the formatted "%02d.ogg" name and gives up on the track when the result is below 1. It forwards to FUN_00481A80(nullptr, name), which returns the cached entry's size (+0x10) or the on-disk size and has no side effects; the same query sizes wave files elsewhere. OpenShimSetMusicTrack uses it to refuse a track that does not exist before touching the engine's music state.

SelectedTrack.description: Selected soundtrack track global. Decode the cmp eax,[abs32] operand at Music::SelectTrack+8, which compares the requested track before deciding whether to call Stop; the final store in the same selector writes that same global. Start formats it as %02d.ogg and the playlist advancer updates it. This is the selected track, not proof of playing, and Stop retains it.
